verdict: Lennar's profit fell by more than half to $284M as higher mortgage rates cooled demand — deliveries slipped 3%, new orders fell 9%, and the gross margin on home sales narrowed to 15.8%.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: total revenue vs a year ago

kpis.label: Home sales gross margin
kpis.note: down from about 17.5% a year ago

segments.name: Homebuilding
segments.note: Building and selling homes: $7,734M of home sales (20,840 deliveries at an average price of about $372,000), plus $18M of land sales and $7M of other homebuilding revenue.

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.note: Mortgages, title and escrow for Lennar's buyers — down 28% on lower lock volume and lower profit per loan.

segments.name: Multifamily
segments.note: Apartment development — revenue fell from $228M a year ago, when more properties were sold.

opex.name: Homebuilding SG&A
opex.note: Selling and running the homebuilding operation — 9.2% of home sales revenue.

opex.name: Financial Services costs
opex.note: The cost of running the mortgage, title and escrow businesses (this line benefited from a one-time litigation accrual reversal).

opex.name: Lennar Other costs
opex.note: Costs of the technology and other ventures.

opex.name: Corporate G&A
opex.note: Head-office general and administrative costs not charged to the segments.

opex.name: Charitable contribution
opex.note: The quarterly contribution to the Lennar Foundation.

otherDetail: A net $73M drag below operating profit (figures rounded): $53M of mark-to-market losses on technology investments, $20M of homebuilding other expense and $4M of Lennar Other equity and other losses, partly offset by $5M of homebuilding equity earnings from unconsolidated entities. A further $1M of earnings went to noncontrolling interests, so the bottom line is the $284M attributable to Lennar.

takeaways.title: Profit more than halved
takeaways.text: Net earnings fell to $284M ($1.19 per share) from $591M ($2.29) a year ago. With the 30-year mortgage rate near 6.8% at quarter-end, Lennar kept volume up with incentives — which protected deliveries but squeezed profit per home.

takeaways.title: Margins are the story
takeaways.text: The gross margin on home sales was 15.8%, down from about 17.5% a year ago, even as construction cost per square foot improved 6% year over year and build cycle time hit a record-low 116 days.

takeaways.title: Orders fell 9%
takeaways.text: New orders dropped 9% to 20,879 homes, and the backlog stands at 16,857 homes worth $6.3B — a thinner cushion if high rates keep buyers on the sidelines.

oneTimers: Lennar Other lost $84M, driven by $53M of mark-to-market losses on technology investments (a year ago the same line gained $99M).
Financial Services costs include $39M, net, of one-time items, primarily a litigation accrual reversal from a favorable court judgment — a benefit, not a cost.
Excluding the technology-investment losses and the Financial Services one-time items, net earnings were $294M ($1.23 per share) versus $284M ($1.19) GAAP.
footerNote: Lennar's fiscal third quarter ended August 31, 2026. Lennar reports costs by segment rather than one cost-of-revenue line: cost of revenue here is costs of homes and land sold ($6,528M), and segment costs plus corporate G&A and the charitable contribution make up operating expenses. Figures are rounded to $M from Lennar's thousands-denominated tables — homebuilding revenue is shown as $7,760M (reported $7,759M) so the rounded segments sum to total revenue. Net earnings are the $284M attributable to Lennar; consolidated net earnings were $285M.
